Marathon Petroleum stock has fallen 1.5% over two weeks and declined slightly again today, tracking a broader slide since late November. The main driver is oil prices: US crude has dropped to $89.53 per barrel from above $100 just weeks ago, which directly erodes refinery margins (the profit refiners make by turning crude into fuel). Refineries are running at 95.7% capacity—near maximum—so there's limited room to boost profits through higher throughput, leaving them exposed to commodity price swings.

The backdrop is a shift in market focus away from energy supply fears. Earlier concerns about Middle Eastern conflict disrupting the Strait of Hormuz have faded from headlines, and looser financial conditions are redirecting investor attention toward technology (data centers, quantum computing) rather than fossil fuels. With oil storage at comfortable levels (694 million barrels) and no acute supply crunch, the near-term narrative no longer supports higher energy prices or refiner valuations.
